title: Diseño y fabricación de adoquines y baldosas de hormigón permeable: diseño y fabricación de adoquines de hormigón permeable.

DC.creator: Oscullo Quishpe, Daniel Josias
DCTERMS.bibliographicCitation: Oscullo Quishpe, D.J. (2025). Diseño y fabricación de adoquines y baldosas de hormigón permeable: diseño y fabricación de adoquines de hormigón permeable. 104 páginas. Quito : EPN.
DC.description: La gestión del agua de lluvia en entornos urbanos enfrenta desafíos crecientes, lo que impulsa la búsqueda de soluciones sostenibles como los adoquines de hormigón permeable. Estos elementos de infraestructura innovadora mitigan la escorrentía superficial y el riesgo de inundaciones, al tiempo que promueven la recarga de acuíferos y mejoran la calidad del agua. La investigación tuvo como objetivo validar el rendimiento, la durabilidad y la viabilidad de estos adoquines, optimizando la mezcla para evaluar sus propiedades mecánicas e hidráulicas. El método de investigación se basó en el diseño y la producción artesanal de adoquines permeables, siguiendo las directrices de la normativa ACI 522-10R. Se estableció una dosificación precisa de agregado grueso, cemento y una relación agua/cemento controlada, empleando materiales específicos y un riguroso proceso de fabricación. Los resultados demuestran un rendimiento hidráulico excepcional de los adoquines permeables en comparación con los convencionales, validando su potencial como una propuesta viable y duradera para la regulación de precipitaciones en áreas urbanas. Su alta eficiencia en la infiltración y una mínima escorrentía, incluso en condiciones de inclinación, los posicionan como una alternativa funcional y sostenible para la infraestructura urbana.
DCTERMS.abstract: Rainwater management in urban environments faces increasing challenges, driving the search for sustainable solutions such as permeable concrete pavers. These innovative infrastructure elements mitigate surface runoff and flood risk while promoting aquifer recharge and improving water quality. The research aimed to validate the performance, durability, and viability of these pavers, optimizing the mix to evaluate their mechanical and hydraulic properties. The research method was based on the design and artisanal production of permeable pavers, following the guidelines of ACI 522-10R. A precise dosage of coarse aggregate, cement, and a controlled water/cement ratio were developed, employing specific materials and a rigorous manufacturing process. The results demonstrate the exceptional hydraulic performance of permeable pavers compared to conventional pavers, validating their potential as a viable and durable solution for rainfall regulation in urban areas. Their high infiltration efficiency and minimal runoff, even under sloping conditions, position them as a functional and sustainable alternative for urban infrastructure.

title: IS THERE A MARKET FOR SELF-HEALING CEMENT- BASED MATERIALS?

meta.pdfText:
Proceedings of the First International Conference on Self Healing Materials
18-20 April 2007, Noordwijk aan Zee, The Netherlands

K. van Breugel

IS THERE A MARKET FOR SELF-HEALING CEMENTBASED MATERIALS?
K. van Breugel
Delft University of Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences/ Microlab,
Delft, The Netherlands
+31 15 2784954 / +31 15 2786383
K.vanbreugel@tudelft.nl
Cement-based building materials are, by definition, made of cement. Cement particles react with water
Producing hydration products. These products “glue” cement and aggregate particles together to a cement paste,
mortar or concrete. The resulting material is a brittle system, susceptible to cracking under external loads and/or
imposed deformations. Cracks are supposed, and known, to jeopardize the strength, stiffness, durability and
service life of concrete structures. The majority of degradation studies reveal that transport processes in concrete
are the main cause of durability problems. The presence of cracks will increase the transport of aggressive
substances into the concrete, thus increasing the risk of degradation of the material. Given the relatively high
brittleness of cement-based systems the formation of cracks is almost unavoidable. If it were possible to close or
fill these cracks through a self-healing mechanism the service life of concrete structures could increase
substantially.
In this contribution examples are presented of proven and potential self-healing of cement-based materials. It
will be explained how the heterogeneous nature of cement-based systems can be considered as an asset when it
comes to realization of built-in self-healing features. In this respect concrete can be considered as a material
different from other building materials since heterogeneity-induced cracking can be considered as an inherent
feature of concrete. This unavoidable cracking is, as far as its consequences for the performance of the material
are concerned, allowed for in all codes implicitly by well-documented material factors. If this cracking could be
used as trigger for starting, or intensifying, a self-healing process, the magnitude of material factors could be
reduced, thus reducing building costs and saving raw materials. Finally it will be mentioned briefly that selfhealing could contribute to better esthetic performance of concrete.

Keywords: Self-healing, self-repair, self-healing concepts, materials design, market,
sustainability, benefits

1

Introduction

Today self-healing is “hot”. This seems to be the case in various fields, particularly in those
fields that have the name to be high-tech. Self-healing materials are also named smart or hightech materials. Building materials, however, are generally bulk materials and qualified as lowtech. Concrete, the most widely used man-made building material, is one of these bulk
materials. Although low-tech it is, as will be discussed later, an extremely complex material.

title: Prediction of concrete pumping performance based on the evaluation of lubrication layer properties = 윤활층 특성의 평가에 의한 콘크리트 펌프압송 성능 예측

DC.creator: 최명성
Choi, Myoung-Sung
DCTERMS.abstract: In this dissertation, to propose prediction methods for the concrete pumping performance in the pipe, the properties of lubrication layer which is a dominant role in concrete pumping were evaluated. In order to predict the concrete pumping performance, the concrete flow typology within a pumping pipe should be carefully analyzed. When concrete is being transported in the pipe, the lubrication layer which forms in the vicinity between the concrete and pipe wall plays a critical role to facilitate the concrete pumping. Therefore, the mechanism for this layer formation is basically investigated with shear induced particle migration and investigated the particle concentration properties along the pipe diameter to quantitatively estimate the properties of lubrication layer. The change of particle concentration can result in different rheological properties in the concrete mixtures and it might influence the concrete flow conditions in the pipe. To demonstrate the effect of particle concentration distribution, various suspension models are used to simulate the concrete pumping condition. The concrete constituents, especially sand and gravel, have angular and irregular shapes that can cause different flow conditions. To consider the particle shape effects on numerical simulation, the intrinsic viscosity concept which measures the effect of individual particles shape on viscosity is used to simulate precisely the shear induced particle migration. To determine an optimum intrinsic viscosity considering the particle shape effects, the circularity concept which is one method to represent shape effects is quantified using digital image processing technique.These factors, i.e. rheological properties due to particle concentration changes and particle shape effects, are considered carefully when performing numerical simulations in order to precisely verify the concrete flow in pipe.Along with numerical approach, to estimate analytically the pumping pressure and flow rates...
